facts.text: A behind-the-wheel drive test is one where you control the vehicle while a DMV examiner evaluates your driving skills.

cites.quote: A drive test where you have control of the vehicle and are accompanied by a DMV examiner who is evaluating your driving skills.

facts.text: A BAC of 0.10% means 0.10 grams of alcohol in 100 milliliters of blood.

cites.quote: if your BAC is 0.10%, that means you have 0.10 grams of alcohol in 100 milliliters of blood.

facts.text: The driving performance evaluation (DPE) is the part of the behind-the-wheel test when you drive with a DMV examiner who evaluates your driving skills.

cites.quote: DPE is the portion of the behind-the-wheel drive test when you drive your car with a DMV examiner who evaluates your driving skills.

facts.text: Right-of-way rules determine who may go first when vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists meet on the road.

cites.quote: Helps determine who is allowed to go first in situations where vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists meet on the road.

facts.text: To use the three-second rule, count three seconds after the vehicle ahead passes a fixed point such as a sign; if you pass that point before you finish counting, you are following too closely.

cites.quote: When the vehicle in front of you passes a certain point, such as a sign, count three seconds. If you pass the same point before you finish counting, you are following too closely.

facts.text: A traffic citation (ticket) is an official summons issued by law enforcement for violating a traffic law.

cites.quote: Also known as a ticket, a traffic citation is an official summons issued by law enforcement for violating a traffic law.

facts.text: Vulnerable road users are non-motorized road users such as cyclists, pedestrians, and people with disabilities or reduced mobility using a wheelchair, tricycle, or quadricycle.

cites.quote: VRUs are non-motorized road users, such as cyclists, pedestrians, and persons with disabilities or reduced mobility and orientation using a wheelchair, tricycle, or quadricycle.

facts.text: To yield means to wait, slow down, and be ready to stop if necessary so that vehicles or pedestrians with the right-of-way can proceed.

cites.quote: Yield means to wait for, slow down, and be ready to stop (if necessary) to allow other vehicles or pedestrians who have right-of-way to proceed.
